title: Exploring Foundations
description: Self-study before the official experimentation phase begins. Working through Chip Huyen's AI Engineering, exploring the LLM ecosystem beyond AI chatbots, and completing Coursera courses.

title: Journey Officially Begins
description: Started a formal one-year exploration dedicated to deep, hands-on experimentation with AI — its capabilities, architectures, and potential for transforming organizations and workflows.

title: Getting the Stack Running
description: First weeks of hands-on experimentation: set up local dev environment, learned Git workflows, deployed first projects to GitHub Pages, Vercel, and Netlify.

title: Canadian AI Jobs Report
description: An interactive dashboard analyzing the economic value of Canadian college majors — mapping CIP programs to NOC occupations with AI disruption risk scores, median salaries, and 10-year job growth metrics.

title: Ottawa Recreation Discovery
description: A visual discovery tool and interactive map for parents to find municipal recreation facilities and summer camps in Ottawa by proximity, amenities, and geographical sector.

title: Policy AI Assistants — NIHB + WFA
description: Two RAG-based policy chatbots grounded in real government documentation: one navigating the Non-Insured Health Benefits program, the other advising on Federal Public Service Work Force Adjustment guidelines.

title: Portfolio Site Launched
description: Built and deployed this portfolio to document the journey publicly — complete with live GitHub stats, a digital brain expansion tracker, a projects grid with filtering, and a workflow architecture diagram.

title: Gmail Cleaner CLI
description: A Python command-line tool to clean, organize, and label Gmail inboxes via IMAP.

title: Drug Utilization Dashboard + Retirement Calculator
description: Two analytical tools in quick succession: a monitoring dashboard for drug utilization data in Canada, and a Defined Benefit pension early retirement calculator mapping portfolio and pension timelines.

title: Games Sprint — Debate, n-1, WordString
description: A rapid games sprint building three web apps: a debate facilitator for kids, an anagram word-unscrambling game, and a cozy sewing-themed word puzzle. Complete with high scores synced to Supabase.

title: Mobile Survey Builder — Now Live
description: A DDI-compliant, mobile-first survey design and EQ authoring tool — featuring re-usable metadata components, nested rosters, complex skip logic, bilingual support, and WCAG accessibility.

title: Modular Survey Tools — Analytics & Collection Dashboard
description: Significant expansion: rebranded to Modular Survey Tools and added several new modular tools — Collector (manage surveys and monitor real-time KPIs), Searcher (discover metadata), Migrator (import external surveys into Designer), and the first video in the Training Hub.

title: Modular Survey Tools — Phase 6 Complete
description: Major sprint completing Phase 6.
details: Added matrix/grid question type across schema, engine, designer, and runtime; migrated backend from Hono+SQLite to Supabase (hosted DB + REST, no server to run); patched a privacy bug where exploration-only surveys were wrongly persisting responses. Also set up a vault-to-site content pipeline so the AI Journey timeline is now editable directly from Obsidian.

title: Local CRA-Compliant Bookkeeping App
description: Built a fully offline desktop bookkeeping app for Canadian sole proprietors using Python and Streamlit.
details: The app ingests Costco Mastercard CSV statements, matches receipts via local OCR (Tesseract), and auto-classifies expenses to CRA Form T2125 lines. It calculates GST/HST ITCs, flags audit risks, and runs entirely locally using DuckDB to ensure financial data privacy.

title: Virtual Tutor — Screen-Aware Learning Companion
description: Conceived an AI tutoring assistant that syncs with the user's active screen to provide real-time, catered instructions and learning guidance.
details: Unlike a standard chatbot, this concept centers on a visual companion that observes the active workspace (via screen capture/OCR or editor integration) and dynamically offers context-aware help, tips, and step-by-step explanations tailored to what the user is currently doing on screen.

title: Real Estate Empire — Prototyping Started
description: Started prototyping a real-estate simulation and strategy game mapped directly onto high-fidelity satellite imagery of Ottawa.
details: Choose your starting backstory (from Elgin Street server to Kanata tech worker), scout listings across actual neighborhoods like The Glebe and Westboro, outbid AI competitors in real-time, and manage your cash flow as the game clock ticks.

title: Ottawa Global Benchmark Engine
description: Built a comparative analytics dashboard comparing Ottawa with global peer cities (Austin, Adelaide, Helsinki) across labour, housing, and tech indicators.
details: Uses Statistics Canada CODR API data via an MCP server, along with FRED, ABS, and Statistics Finland. Built with a DuckDB-Wasm backend in the browser for fast, on-the-fly index baseline and divergence trend analysis. Setting up a data pipeline for a major expansion once new census data becomes available.

title: Built Custom Portfolio Editor
description: Created a standalone local editor to manage the portfolio's content, complete with a one-click GitHub publish integration.
details: To streamline workflow documentation, I replaced the hardcoded HTML with a dynamic JSON architecture. The accompanying Editor app allows me to easily add projects and timeline entries, view the Git diff of my changes, and automatically publish to the live site without touching the codebase.

title: Wobbleton — Tower Workshop
description: Built a cozy 3D physics-based tower building sandbox in the browser.
details: First project using Three.js and the Web Audio API. Built a lightweight, custom rigid-body physics engine (sleeping/waking bodies, material stickiness/weight, and soft-sphere collisions) from scratch to simulate structures made of straw, wood, brick, stone, and glass. Test towers against disasters like earthquakes, tornadoes, meteors, and windstorms while generating native procedural lo-fi soundtrack loops and audio effects.

title: Wobbleton — Game Night PWA
description: Completed a mobile-optimized 2-player local party game hub with 12 mini-games.
details: Expanding the 'Wobbleton' design family. Built a collection of 12 distinct competitive mini-games sharing a single screen (including Tug o' Rope, Boxy Toe, Frosty Pond, and Statue Race). Configured full offline-first behavior using a custom Service Worker cache and fixed mobile browser viewport camera scaling issues.

title: Capability Atlas
description: Developed a modular Enterprise Business Architecture (EBA) application for public sector modernization.
details: Built using React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4. Implemented a 3-pass redundancy analyzer (surfacing organizational, semantic text-similarity, and shared-information data-effort overlap) and an automated greedy-packing transition roadmap engine that topologically sequences IT investments against fiscal budgets and compounding efficiency savings. Outputs a fully formatted PDF Business Case dynamically.

title: Kingdoms of Wobbleton — 3D Medieval RTS
description: Re-themed and expanded the Three.js RTS engine into a boxy medieval game.
details: Pivoted to a boxy medieval aesthetic using glTF assets. Implemented procedural seeded maps, deterministic simulation lockstep for online 1v1 play, dynamic fog of war, and synthesized runtime audio.

title: Kingdoms of Wobbleton — Lobbies & Control Upgrades
description: Expanded multiplayer support to 4-player lobbies and implemented strategy controls.
details: Upgraded the Three.js game room structure to support 4 players in lobbies. Implemented classic RTS mechanics including wall building, shift-queueing commands, double-tap control groups, and double-click multi-selection.

title: First Substack Post: Teaching a Machine to File My Thoughts
description: Published my first article on 'Artificially Sociological', reflecting on using agentic AI to build a persistent digital brain.

title: Modular Survey Tools — DDI-Lifecycle 3.3 Compliance
description: Finished compliance updates to DDI-Lifecycle schemas with automated XSD validation tests.
details: Successfully implemented Colectica-compliant FragmentInstance packaging. Verified that real, large-scale (14MB to 66MB) labor force survey XML files from Ireland import with full structural accuracy.

title: Kingdoms of Wobbleton — Hosted Online Play
description: Hosted the multiplayer WebSocket relay on Render to enable public online matches.
details: Deployed the game's relay server to Render, moving the multiplayer matchmaking from local-only networks to public online matchmaking.

title: Open Stats Lab — AI Visibility Experiment Launched
description: Pre-registered and deployed a controlled experiment to test if structured table mirrors improve data visibility for AI search engines.
details: Conducted a 100-query pilot study analyzing how generative AI answers cite statistical agencies. Found that search crawlers ignore dynamic Javascript tables and robots-blocked CSV files, defaulting to stale analytical articles. Deployed static HTML mirror tables with structured schema.org/Dataset markup to measure crawlability differences against control tables over a 12-week period.
